items.title: [Feature]: Add native agent capability router plugin
items.body:
## Problem to solve

Agentic clients shift between planning, implementation, debugging, tool execution, exploration, and summarization within one conversation. Complexity-only routing cannot distinguish those kinds of work, so operators must either use one model for every turn or maintain client-side routing logic.

## Proposed solution

Add an opt-in native `agent-capability-router` pre-request plugin that:

- handles only configured dynamic aliases such as `agent-main-auto` and `agent-worker-auto`;
- deterministically classifies the current capability from recent normalized chat/responses history;
- rewrites only the logical lane (`agent-main-debug`, `agent-worker-implement`, etc.);
- runs before the existing native routing plugin, allowing current `complexity_tier` CEL rules to combine role, capability, and effort;
- never selects a provider or physical model;
- defaults to shadow mode and bypasses all unrelated traffic.

The classifier is stateless, uses only Bifrost's existing dependencies, and includes transition and bypass tests. Existing routing rules remain responsible for providers, targets, and fallback chains.

## Alternatives considered

- Complexity-only routing cannot distinguish architecture, coding, debugging, and tool loops at the same effort tier.
- An LLM classifier adds cost, latency, recursion risk, and nondeterminism.
- Client-side routing duplicates policy across agent clients and weakens gateway ownership.

## Area

Plugins, Transports (HTTP), Docs

## Additional context

A standalone Bifrost v2.0-compatible plugin has already been tested in shadow and active routing modes. This issue proposes the native, ABI-free upstream form.

items.title: feat: resident-aware virtual models
items.body:
## Summary

Adds virtual models: a stable client-facing name that resolves to a concrete model at request time, choosing whichever candidate the backend already holds in memory. The fundamental issue is that naming a model that is *not* loaded on a self-hosted engine is expensive; the backend evicts whatever is resident to fetch it, and the model that was serving
 traffic with a warm KV cache pays for it. Aliases and routing rules cannot express this because the correct target depends on state that only exists at request time.

Fixes #8531

## Changes

   - Added virtual model config, validation and selection in core. A virtual name maps to an ordered list of candidates on one provider.
   - Selection order: first candidate that is ready, else the first one still loading (so a request joins a load already running instead of starting a competing one), else the first model in the list. **If none of the candidates are resident, Bifrost sends the first model ("preferred") and lets the backend load it.** That can evict whatever else is resident, so it is worth being explicit about.
   - Added residency readers for oMLX, llama.cpp and ollama, plus a custom field mapping for engines we have no adapter for. Auto-detect tries them in that order and remembers which one answered.
   - The endpoints were measured. oMLX uses /v1/models/status (loaded/is_loading), llama.cpp uses /v1/models (status.value; /props reported model_path "none" while a model was loaded, so it is not usable), and ollama uses its native /api/ps because its OpenAI /v1/models has no residency field at all. ollama is last on purpose: an empty process list on an idle machine would otherwise look like a good probe and hide the other engines.
   - Resolution runs in core, after the routing plugins and before session routing and key selection. Governance keeps first refusal on the name the client sent, and keys filter on the model that will actually serve. It is not a plugin because RunPreRequestHooks logs hook errors and carries on, so a plugin cannot block a request it should not route.
   - Virtual names are listed in /v1/models and /api/models, and /v1/models/{name} is answered by Bifrost with live residency. Listings do not probe: a /v1/models that fanned out to every backend turns a metadata call into a residency read of every GPU on the network.
   - A provider says how to read its residency with `model_residency` (adapter, path, timeout_ms, cache_ttl_ms, fields). It is wired into `transports/config.schema.json` on every provider shape, so the documented setting validates instead of being rejected by the schema.
   - A virtual model never shadows a real model that shares its name. A provider named explicitly, by path prefix or `?provider=`, outranks the virtual name and the request goes to that provider untouched, so `provider/model` stays the way to pin a vendor and a virtual model can be named after a vendor model without hiding it. The comparison folds case, since
 virtual models store the owning provider lowercased.
   - Access to a virtual name is derived from its candidates rather than asserted, and a virtual entry publishes `accessible_by_keys` with that result.
   - Trade-offs: no automatic fallback chain (a stale pick normally cold-loads rather than 404ing, so a chain adds loads without fresher data), one provider per virtual model, and config file only with no dashboard CRUD yet.

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [x] Documentation
- [ ] Chore/CI

## Affected areas

- [x] Core (Go)
- [x] Transports (HTTP)
- [ ] Providers/Integrations
- [ ] Plugins
- [ ] UI (React)
- [x] Docs

I built the full UI and Go binary in a disposable container and tested end to end against three engines on one Apple Silicon box sharing unified memory — oMLX (chat), llama.cpp (chat + embeddings), ollama (chat). 

Tested end to end against three engines on one Apple Silicon box sharing unified memory: oMLX (chat), llama.cpp (chat and embeddings) and ollama (chat). Each engine ran one at a time and returned to its prior state. Every response reported the concrete model with routing_info.requested_model keeping the virtual name. The unit fixtures for the readers are the payloads recorded from those engines.

 New configuration (all documented in docs/providers/virtualmodels.mdx):

 ```json
   "virtual_models": {
     "local-chat": {
       "provider": "local-omlx",     // required; must be a configured provider
       "models": ["preferred", "alternate"],  // preference order, required, non-empty
       "on_probe_error": "error"     // error (default) | first
     }
   }
 ```


## Screenshots/Recordings

NA

items.title: feat(plugins): add cache-aware prompt_compression plugin
items.body:
## Summary

Adds `prompt_compression`, an opt-in built-in plugin that cuts input tokens in agent loops by shortening **old** tool outputs (file reads, test logs, search results the model has already used). It keeps edits stable across turns so provider prompt caching is not broken by repeated rewrites, and fails open: any error sends the original request. It works on the neutral Chat Completions and Responses shapes, so requests that reach the plugin as Chat or Responses can benefit; see the caching trade-offs and limitations.

Proposed in #9617. Built as part of the Geek Room AI Hackathon (Bifrost track).

## Changes

- **`plugins/promptcompression`** (new module, `PreLLMHook`/`PostLLMHook`). It edits only **eligible** outputs: `tool` messages (Chat) and `function_call_output` items (Responses) that are outside the cache-protected prefix and at least `tool_output_min_age_turns` assistant turns old (default 2, minimum 1). Three strategies:
  1. **Trim:** eligible outputs of at least `tool_output_min_tokens` estimated tokens (default 500) keep their first and last N lines, with `[… N tokens trimmed by promptcompression …]` in between. Trimming is idempotent.
  2. **Dedupe:** an older identical output becomes `[identical to the output of call <id>]`, pointing at the next newer copy. The decision is made once, when the older copy becomes eligible, and only if the newer copy already existed then; a duplicate that arrives later never rewrites an output that was already sent.
  3. **Whitespace:** trailing spaces and runs of 3+ blank lines are cleaned in eligible outputs only. An output is never emptied.
- **Guarantees** (each covered by tests):
  - No message is removed or reordered; roles and tool-call IDs are untouched.
  - **Stability:** while the client's cache-protected prefix does not move, every edit already made stays as it was (and untouched messages stay untouched); the only new edits are at outputs that just became old enough. If a client moves a cache marker forward, outputs inside the newly protected prefix go back to the client's text and edits outside it stay as they were. Only a non-zero `min_savings_tokens`, or a Responses request that ends on an assistant prefill, can change an edit that was already made.
  - The cache-protected prefix (client markers: `cache_control`, `prompt_cache_breakpoint`, Bedrock `cachePoint`, Responses message/block markers) stays byte-identical.
  - Requests with request-level `cache_control` are not touched: Chat (`cache_control` param) and Responses (`cache_control` in extra params, e.g. the Anthropic SDK on `/anthropic/v1/messages`).
  - An edit is kept only if it is strictly shorter, so a compressed request is always strictly smaller in bytes. The new `min_savings_tokens` threshold (default 0) is measured over the eligible outputs only.
  - The incoming request is never mutated (copy-on-write); a panic sends the original request.
  - Skipped: other request types, raw-body passthrough, large-payload mode.
- **Observability:** one Info line per compressed request (on the final chunk for streams, Chat and Responses): `request_id`, `estimated_before`, `estimated_after`, `prompt_tokens`, `cached_read_tokens`. Context values are cleared after logging so reused contexts never log stale numbers.
- **Gateway:** registered as a built-in at order 10, after `semanticcache` (so cache hits skip compression) and after `logging` (order 3, which therefore shows the original messages; its token usage and cost come from provider-reported usage and reflect what was sent). Added to `builtinPluginNames`; the config is in `config.schema.json`.
- **Docs:** `docs/features/plugins/prompt-compression.mdx`.
- **Tooling:** `benchmark/estimates.md` (offline per-turn estimates), `benchmark/run.mjs` (live replay script, **not run**), harness folder **310** in `provider-harness.json`.

**Caching trade-offs (stated in the docs):**
- Clients that mark the latest message every turn protect the whole conversation, so the plugin does nothing for them. Clients that move a marker forward keep hitting the provider's cached prefix: outputs inside the new prefix revert to the client's text, and edits outside it stay byte-identical.
- With automatic prefix caching (no markers), an edit at the output that just aged past the threshold re-bills the cached part after it. **Steady state:** every request re-bills the cached content after the newest edit, roughly the last `tool_output_min_age_turns` turns.
- Bifrost's own provider `prompt_cache` injection is applied after plugins and is invisible to the plugin. Do not combine the plugin with injection at the last message (`index: -1`, or a `role: user` point, which also matches tool results); prefer `auto_inject` or a system-prompt point.
- A non-zero `min_savings_tokens` can switch compression on late and off again when a client moves a cache marker; that is why the default is 0.

**Limitations (stated in the docs):** raw-body passthrough is skipped (Claude Code requests to Claude models normally, with OAuth or API key; raw passthrough is turned off only for providers that need synthetic structured output when the request carries `output_config.format`, and on Vertex only with the prompt-caching-scope or fast-mode beta headers; `/genai` with an explicit Gemini model); only `function_call_output` / `tool` outputs are compressed; trimmed JSON can be cut mid-structure; the logging plugin shows the original messages, while its usage and cost reflect what was sent; requests ending on an assistant message or prefill can shift Responses turn counts.

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [x] Documentation
- [ ] Chore/CI

## Affected areas

- [ ] Core (Go)
- [x] Transports (HTTP)
- [ ] Providers/Integrations
- [x] Plugins
- [ ] UI (React)
- [x] Docs

## Cost statement (AGENTS.md)

`go test -run '^$' -bench PreLLMHook -benchmem -count=3 ./...` (i7-1265U), median of 3 runs, on the same machine. "Before" is the base revision of this PR (cb10905dd), "after" is the current HEAD (after the zero-token fix and cleanups). The two columns come from two separate sessions on that machine; in one session where both revisions were benchmarked back to back, the ratios were the same (e.g. small chat 866 ns vs 110 ns).

| Case | before ns/op | before B/op | before allocs | after ns/op | after B/op | after allocs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Plugin disabled | not registered: **zero cost** | 0 | 0 | not registered: **zero cost** | 0 | 0 |
| Enabled, other request type (e.g. embeddings) | ~10.5-11 | 0 | 0 | 9.6 | 0 | 0 |
| Enabled, small chat with nothing to compress | 866 | 704 | 3 | 107 | 0 | 0 |
| Enabled, nothing old enough to edit, tool rounds present (Chat) | n/a | n/a | n/a | 128 | 0 | 0 |
| Enabled, nothing old enough to edit, tool rounds present (Responses) | n/a | n/a | n/a | 185 | 0 | 0 |
| Enabled, 12-round agent session (Chat) | ~110,000 | 61,449 | 73 | 26,743 | 9,952 | 42 |
| Enabled, 12-round agent session (Responses) | ~121,000 | 67,454 | 77 | 33,358 | 15,957 | 46 |
| Enabled, 100-round ~800 KB mixed history (Chat) | n/a | n/a | n/a | 389,456 | 162,943 | 457 |
| Enabled, 100-round ~800 KB mixed history (Responses) | n/a | n/a | n/a | 454,473 | 224,367 | 541 |

- Cost grows with the conversation's text size. Zero allocations applies when nothing is eligible (a first pass decides whether any edit is possible and returns the original request untouched). With eligible but clean outputs the dedupe plan may allocate a small map (about 7 allocations measured).
- "n/a" means the benchmark did not exist at the base revision.
- Absolute ns/op on this laptop varied by up to about 2x between sessions; B/op and allocs/op are exact and reproducible.
- **Retained memory:** none beyond the request (two ints and a bool in the request context, cleared after logging). No caches or managers.

## Savings (estimates only)

These are chars÷4 estimates on a synthetic 12-round coding-agent fixture (`plugins/promptcompression/testdata`). They are **not** provider-measured, and cache effects are not modelled.

| | Estimated input tokens |
|---|---|
| All 13 requests, total | 88,399 → 32,352 (**63.4 %**) |
| Mean saving per request | **46.8 %** (0 % for the first 4 requests, ~80 % from request 9) |

These replace the earlier figures (64.9 % total, 47.9 % mean), which were computed before edits were limited to eligible outputs.

`plugins/promptcompression/benchmark/run.mjs` replays the same session through a running gateway, with the plugin off and then on, and reports real `prompt_tokens`/`cached_tokens`. **I have not run it** (no paid provider calls on my side), so provider-measured savings and cache behaviour are unverified.

## How to test

```sh
cd plugins/promptcompression
go test -race ./... && go vet ./...
go test -v -run 'Fixture|PerTurn' ./...      # prints the estimates
go test -run '^$' -bench PreLLMHook -benchmem -count=3 ./...
cd ../..
go test ./transports/bifrost-http/server/ -run PromptCompression
```

Enable it with:

```json
{ "name": "prompt_compression", "enabled": true }
```

All config fields are optional and listed in the docs and the schema.

**Provider harness:** folder 310 enables the plugin through `POST /api/plugins`, sends a chat completion and a `/v1/responses` request (with a tools array and large old tool outputs), asserts 200 plus the response shape, and then deletes the plugin row. It now also asserts that `usage.prompt_tokens` / `input_tokens` is **below 34,000**. The same session is about 58,845 estimated tokens uncompressed and about 20,593 compressed, so the bound sits 1.65x above the compressed estimate and 1.73x below the uncompressed one: the case fails when the plugin is off (the previous version passed either way). It needs a config store. Validated structurally only (`augment-provider-harness.mjs` + `filter-collection.mjs --feature prompt-compression`). **I did not run it live.** Commands:

```sh
docker compose -f tests/docker-compose.yml up -d weaviate
until curl -sf http://localhost:9000/v1/.well-known/ready >/dev/null && nc -z localhost 50051; do sleep 2; done
make dev PORT=8181 APP_DIR=$(pwd)/tests/integrations/python
make run-provider-harness-test PROVIDER=openai FEATURE="prompt-compression" BASE_URL=http://localhost:8181
```

The live run costs about 2 gpt-4o-mini calls of ~20k input tokens each.

**Routes:**
- `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/responses` have harness cases.
- `/anthropic/v1/messages`, `/bedrock` and `/genai` reach the plugin through the neutral Chat/Responses types but have **no harness case**. The plugin sees only the neutral `Input` (it never reads provider headers or a native body), and the shape it edits is the same one the two covered routes carry; a native-route case would test the SDK converters rather than this plugin, and Claude Code traffic on `/anthropic/v1/messages` is raw passthrough, which is skipped by design. Unit tests drive Chat and Responses inputs, including the `cache_control` extra-param path that `/anthropic/v1/messages` produces. A live case for these routes would also need paid Anthropic, Bedrock and Gemini calls.
- Raw-body passthrough (Claude Code requests to Claude models, normally, with OAuth or API key; `/genai` with an explicit Gemini model) is skipped by design, so the flagship Claude Code case is not compressed.

## Breaking changes

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

The plugin is opt-in and not registered unless enabled.

## Related issues

Closes #9617

## Notes for maintainers

- **`transports/go.mod`:** I added no `require` for the new module. The precedent is the routing plugin (#6144, then 57506223d), which needs a pseudo-version of a commit in `maximhq/bifrost`, and that only exists after merge. Local builds resolve the module through `go.work` (`make setup-workspace`). Please add `github.com/maximhq/bifrost/plugins/promptcompression <version>` before the next transports release.
- **Log level:** the savings line is Info. Happy to switch it to Debug or make it configurable if that suits high-RPS deployments better.
- Harness folder number 310 may need renumbering if another PR takes it first.

## Changes since review

Review findings (an independent code review, a second independent review, and CodeRabbit) and where each is addressed:

| Finding | Commit(s) |
|---|---|
| A. Dedupe rewrote deep, already-cached history | `c590ebaa0` (decision fixed at eligibility time), `795a32d23` and `44977e4ad` (edits only on eligible outputs), `0b3ba0406` (cross-turn prefix stability test) |
| B. Anthropic automatic caching on `/anthropic/v1/messages` not detected | `8c765c012` (Responses `cache_control` in extra params skips compression) |
| C. Bifrost `prompt_cache` injection invisible to the plugin | `1b220b3b0` (trade-offs section, recommended setup) |
| D. `min_savings_percent` flapped | `8c765c012` (measured on the eligible region), `116e369e6` (absolute `min_savings_tokens`), `988591a9a` (default 0), `5cad999e5` (threshold-pressure tests) |
| E. Responses turn counting | `44977e4ad` (every model-produced item is part of a turn), `dd6ee2a0d` (approval/config/tool-search items classified correctly) |
| F. Hot path on long histories | `41e2a5cd2` (split-free checks), `0d576e21f` (whitespace fast path matches the slow path), `795a32d23` and `44977e4ad` (no-alloc first pass, lazy output), `0b3ba0406` (large-history benchmark) |
| G. Harness 310 could not detect the feature; uncovered routes unexplained | `7e6112b24` (token-bound assertion, tools arrays); routes explained above |
| H. Docs and PR overstated reach | `1b220b3b0` and `dd4dd7d90` (passthrough reach, steady-state re-bill, stability and logging wording); this description |
| m1. Whitespace-only output became empty | `41e2a5cd2` |
| m2. Trim not idempotent | `41e2a5cd2` |
| m3. Streamed Responses logged `prompt_tokens=0` | `8c765c012` |
| m4. `tool_output_min_age_turns: 0` | `8c765c012` (rejected at startup), `1b220b3b0` (schema `minimum: 1`) |
| m5. No request id in the log line; logging shows the original messages | `8c765c012` (request id), `1b220b3b0` and `dd4dd7d90` (note) |
| m6. "tokens" wording | `1b220b3b0` (bytes ÷ 4, rounded up) |
| m7. `run.mjs` robustness | `7e6112b24` |
| m8. Spec example name | design spec (not in this repo) |
| Final review C1. Zero-token whitespace edits switched compression off and on, so earlier edits appeared late | `df8fbe653` (compress iff changed and saved >= `min_savings_tokens`; tests `TestHookZeroTokenEditStaysStable`, `TestHookMovingCacheMarkerZeroTokenEdit`) |
| Final review I1, I2, M2, M3. Stability and passthrough wording, allocation claim, no-op tests | `e0062b1e5` (docs), `3c335177a` (zero-alloc no-op cases, Responses no-op benchmark) |
| Follow-up: a dedupe stub replacing many tiny text blocks could estimate larger than the blocks (negative saving), so the default threshold held the edit back and it appeared late. The threshold now applies only when `min_savings_tokens` > 0 (regression test `TestHookNegativeSavingStaysStable`) | `6b6764f5c` |
| Follow-up: duplicated sentence in the moving-marker docs bullet | `f043cfe10` |
| Final review M1, T1, T2. Dead code, comment, shadowing type | `3c335177a` |

**Config change: `min_savings_percent` replaced by `min_savings_tokens`.** A percentage over the eligible region still moved with the request: one large fresh payload or a growing history changed the ratio, so a request could drop below the threshold, send the original, revert every earlier edit and bust the cached prefix twice. An absolute token count over the eligible outputs only never decreases while the client's prefix is stable, and at the default 0 compression stays on once it is on: every edit is sent, including zero-token whitespace edits, so a request with any edit is always strictly smaller in bytes. An old `min_savings_percent` key is ignored by the plugin's config decoding but rejected by the JSON schema (`additionalProperties: false`). The schema entry is `min_savings_tokens` (integer, minimum 0, default 0).

## Security considerations

None. No secrets, auth or network calls. The plugin only shortens text the client already sent, and only in old tool outputs. Fixture content is synthetic.

## Checklist

- [x] I read `docs/contributing/README.md` and followed the guidelines
- [x] I added/updated tests where appropriate
- [x] I updated documentation where needed
- [x] I verified builds succeed (Go and UI): Go plugin and transports build locally with `go.work`; UI untouched
- [ ] I verified the CI pipeline passes locally if applicable

**AI use:** designed and implemented with Claude Code (spec → plan → per-task implementation with an independent review of each task), using the Bifrost docs MCP and the repo's `.claude/skills`. Every change was reviewed and tested before this PR.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

items.title: ci: run live provider calls through real http, https and socks5 proxies
items.body:
## Summary

Adds a `test-proxy-e2e` CI job that validates Bifrost's proxy support by making real provider calls through real forward proxies. This catches the class of failure a customer behind a corporate proxy experiences — TLS errors or silent timeouts — before a release ships.

## Changes

- **New `test-proxy-e2e` CI job** in `release-pipeline.yml`: boots squid (HTTP), stunnel in front of squid (HTTPS/TLS-to-proxy), and microsocks (SOCKS5), all requiring credentials, then runs one cell per combination of proxy mode (global, per-provider `proxy_config`, environment `HTTPS_PROXY`) and proxy protocol. Triggered on core, framework, and bifrost-http changes, and gated as a required check on all downstream release jobs.

- **`tests/e2e/api/runners/proxy/run-proxy-matrix.sh`**: the matrix runner. Each cell boots a fresh gateway, runs the provider harness against `proxy-smoke-manifest.json`, then asserts every provider's hostname appeared in that cell's proxy log and not on the infra proxy port. Supports `RERUN_ATTEMPTS` for flaky rows and `PROXY_E2E_STRICT_EGRESS=1` to confine the gateway to loopback via `iptables --gid-owner`, so a request that skips the proxy fails outright rather than silently going direct.

- **`tests/e2e/api/runners/proxy/proxy-lib.sh`**: sourceable helpers that generate a CA and proxy certificate, write squid/stunnel/microsocks configs, start and stop the three proxies, self-check that each refuses anonymous clients (a proxy that allows anonymous traffic would make every credential test a no-op), and expose log-reading functions (`proxy_hosts_on_port`, `proxy_socks_hosts`, `proxy_tls_sessions`).

- **`tests/e2e/api/collections/proxy-smoke-manifest.json`**: one upstream-reaching harness row per provider (23 total), each the cheapest existing row that proves egress. Includes `hosts` patterns (extended regexes) that `run-proxy-matrix.sh` matches against the proxy access log.

- **New harness collection folder 118** in `provider-harness.json`: cheap `/v1/models` rows for nebius and elevenlabs, which had no other inexpensive upstream-reaching row to reference from the manifest.

- **`harness-gateway.sh` extended**: `HARNESS_BINARY` is now overridable (so bifrost-enterprise can pass its own licensed binary with `SKIP_GATEWAY_BUILD=1`). `harness_start_gateway` accepts `HARNESS_GATEWAY_ENV` (environment variables set only in the gateway process) and `HARNESS_GATEWAY_GROUP` (runs the gateway under a specific group via `sg` so the `iptables --gid-owner` rule confines only it).

- **`test-proxy-e2e.sh`**: thin CI wrapper that sets `PROXY_E2E_STRICT_EGRESS=1` and delegates to `run-proxy-matrix.sh`.

- **`check-egress-allowlist.sh`**: `test-proxy-e2e.sh` added to `HARNESS_MARKERS` so the egress allowlist checker recognises it as a provider-harness job.

- **`Makefile`**: `run-e2e-api PROXY=1` runs the proxy matrix locally (installs squid, stunnel, microsocks first). `run-e2e-api-proxy` is a convenience alias. `install-squid` and `install-stunnel` targets added.

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Chore/CI

## Affected areas

- [ ] Core (Go)
- [x] Transports (HTTP)
- [x] Providers/Integrations
- [ ] Plugins
- [ ] UI (React)
- [ ] Docs

## How to test

```sh
# Run the full proxy matrix locally (loads secrets from Infisical or .env)
make run-e2e-api-proxy

# Run only specific cells
PROXY_CELLS="provider-http env-socks5" make run-e2e-api PROXY=1

# Run with strict egress (Linux only, requires sudo)
PROXY_E2E_STRICT_EGRESS=1 make run-e2e-api PROXY=1
```

Per-cell Newman reports, gateway logs, and proxy access logs are written to `tmp/proxy-e2e/cells/<cell>/`.

## Breaking changes

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Security considerations

- The proxy password is generated fresh each run (`openssl rand -hex 12`) and never leaves the runner.
- `BEDROCK_GUARDRAIL_VERSION` is stored as a repository variable rather than a secret because Actions masks secret values globally with no word boundary — a value of `"1"` would redact every `"1"` in the job log. The guardrail version is not sensitive.
- Strict egress uses `iptables --gid-owner` to confine only the gateway process group, leaving the rest of the runner's network unrestricted.

## Checklist

- [x] I read `docs/contributing/README.md` and followed the guidelines
- [x] I added/updated tests where appropriate
- [x] I updated documentation where needed
- [x] I verified builds succeed (Go and UI)
- [x] I verified the CI pipeline passes locally if applicable

items.body:
## Summary

`network_config.base_url` sits alongside config fields that already accept a `SecretVar` reference (`ca_cert_pem`, `proxy.url`, the Ollama/SGL key URLs), but a `"base_url": "env.SOME_VAR"` was never resolved: it was passed through and dialed as a literal hostname. Requests to that provider fail to connect with no diagnostic pointing at the real problem.

This makes `base_url` a `SecretVar` like the other reference-capable fields, so an upstream URL can be kept out of committed config the same way credentials already can.

## Changes

- `NetworkConfig.BaseURL` is now `*schemas.SecretVar` (`json:"base_url"`), the same shape as `CACertPEM` and `ProxyConfig.URL`. `SecretVar.UnmarshalJSON` handles plain URLs, `env.`, and `vault.` references; `MarshalJSON` emits `SecretVarAsString(nc.BaseURL)`, so config-store persistence, `ProviderConfig` hashing, and API responses stay reference-shaped. No shadow field.
- Every read site goes through `BaseURL.GetValue()`: all providers (including `databricks` and `github-copilot`, which landed on `dev` after this PR was opened), the OpenAI/ElevenLabs realtime paths, and the provider HTTP handler's `ValidateExternalURL` check.
- The per-provider default-URL / trailing-slash block in every constructor is folded into one `providerUtils.NormalizeBaseURL(&config.NetworkConfig, defaultURL)` helper (`""` for ollama, sgl, vllm, databricks, and github-copilot, whose base URL is optional). It clones the `SecretVar` before trimming, so a pointer shared with a config-store copy is never mutated in place, and the `env.`/`vault.` reference survives normalization.
- Fail-loud at decode on a reference that resolves to an empty value: `network_config.base_url references "env.X" but it resolved to an empty value`. Same fail-closed stance `ConfigureTLS` takes for `ca_cert_pem`; the alternative is dialing an empty host. Surrounding whitespace in a resolved value is trimmed.
- The ollama/sgl key-backfill migration copies the `SecretVar` into the key URL (reference preserved) instead of wrapping the resolved string.
- `config.schema.json`: `base_url` documents the reference form and drops `"format": "uri"`, which an `env.` reference would not satisfy. The wire form is still a string, so the UI types are unaffected.
- One line in `docs/quickstart/gateway/provider-configuration.mdx`.
- Review follow-ups (third commit): `NetworkConfig.Redacted` clones `BaseURL` and masks the resolved value when it came from a reference (literal URLs stay readable for the UI); `providerUtils.LoggableURL` keeps a reference-resolved base URL out of the four Gemini batch debug logs.
- UI (second commit): the provider network form, the provider-form schema, and the custom-provider sheet previously rejected anything that was not a URL. One shared `isValidBaseURL` predicate (http(s) URL or a non-empty `env.`/`vault.` reference) now backs all four validation sites via `baseURLSchema`, and the base URL inputs describe the reference form. Wire shape unchanged. Since dev's i18n pass, the validation message and the help text are catalog keys (`validation.validBaseUrlOrSecretReference` in `common`, `providers.network.baseUrlHelp` in `models`) with translations in all 11 locales.

Revision history: v1 hand-rolled `os.LookupEnv` prefix handling; v2 resolved through `SecretVar` but kept `BaseURL` a `string` with a hidden retained reference (reviewer: a workaround); v3 (this) converts the field itself and updates the callers, per review.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

## Affected areas

- [x] Core (Go)
- [x] Framework (configstore migration)
- [x] Transports (provider handler, `config.schema.json`)
- [x] Docs
- [x] UI

## How to test

```sh
# in core/, framework/, transports/ (go.work via `make setup-workspace`)
go build ./... && go vet ./...

cd core && go test -count=1 ./schemas/ ./providers/...
cd transports && go test -count=1 ./bifrost-http/lib/
cd framework && go test -count=1 ./configstore/

# UI
cd ui && npm ci --ignore-scripts && npx vitest run lib/utils/validation.test.ts
```

- `TestNetworkConfig_BaseURLSecretRef` (core/schemas): literal passthrough and round-trip; absent stays nil and is omitted; `env.` resolves, keeps its reference, and round-trips as the reference (never the resolved URL); whitespace trimmed; unset, empty, whitespace-only `env.` and unresolvable `vault.` fail loud.
- `isSecretReference` / `isValidBaseURL` (ui/lib/utils/validation.test.ts): accepts http(s) URLs and `env.`/`vault.` references; rejects bare hosts, non-http schemes, empty references, and `https://env.example.com`-style lookalikes.
- `TestNetworkConfig_Redacted_BaseURL` (core/schemas) and `TestLoggableURL` (core/providers/utils): redacted copies clone and mask reference-resolved base URLs, and debug-log rendering hides the resolved host.
- `TestNormalizeBaseURL` (core/providers/utils): default only when unset; trailing slashes trimmed; `env.` reference retained; caller's `SecretVar` cloned, not mutated; no-op with no default.

Verified locally on Go 1.27 (toolchain auto) against current `dev` @ `03ab39186`: `core`, `framework`, `transports`, and all `plugins/*` build and vet clean; `core` schemas/providers tests, `framework/configstore` tests, and `transports/bifrost-http/lib` tests pass, with one exception: `TestGenerateMCPClientHash_RuntimeVsMigrationParity` fails identically on a clean `dev` checkout and is unrelated to this change. `validate-schema-sync.sh` reports the same three errors on `dev` and on this branch. UI: `vitest` passes for the touched file (the one failing test file in the suite, `logs/views/columns.test.ts`, fails identically on `dev`); `tsc --noEmit` reports no errors in the touched files (the 97 route-typing errors it reports are identical on `dev`); `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` are clean for the touched code.

Re-verified after merging `dev` @ `d5a36220c` (2026-10-31): every workspace module builds and vets clean, and the changed packages' tests pass except ones that fail identically on `dev` (the STDIO MCP tests, `TestMCPSDK`, `TestListAllModelsIncludesEveryPageOfASlowLargeProvider`). UI: `vite build`, `tsc --noEmit`, `oxfmt --check` on the touched files and the full `vitest` suite pass, apart from one catalog-loading test that times out at 5 s on `dev` as well. `npm run i18n:check` reports only the two proxy-URL literals in `ui/lib/types/schemas.ts` that `dev` already has.

## Breaking changes

- [x] Yes, for Go consumers of the `core` module only

`NetworkConfig.BaseURL` changes type from `string` to `*schemas.SecretVar`; downstream Go code reads it with `GetValue()` and sets it with `schemas.NewSecretVar(...)`. The JSON wire form (`config.json`, config store, HTTP API) is unchanged: a plain URL string still works, and `env.`/`vault.` strings that were previously dialed literally now resolve.

## Related issues

Found while migrating a downstream deployment ([LaneTally](https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/lanetally)) from `transports/v1.5.16` to `transports/v2.0.0`.

## Security considerations

Lets operators keep upstream endpoints out of committed config and out of the config store, using the same reference mechanism already trusted for credentials. The resolved URL never appears in marshaled output while the reference still resolves to it.

## Checklist

- [x] I read `docs/contributing/README.md` and followed the guidelines
- [x] I added/updated tests where appropriate
- [x] I verified builds succeed (Go)

items.title: feat(logs): redesign grouped view expander with tree lines, turn/fallback labels, and kind markers
items.body:
## Summary

Improves the grouped log view to visually and semantically distinguish session rows (requests sharing a `session_id`) from fallback chain rows (attempts sharing a `parent_request_id`). Previously both group types rendered identically with a bare count and a chevron. Now each expander uses plain-language labels ("2 turns" vs "1 fallback"), tooltips that name the grouping key, and tree branch lines that connect parent rows to their children. Session member rows are highlighted with a blue left border while chain rows remain grey, so the kind of nesting is readable even when the expand column is scrolled out of view.

## Changes

- Replaced bare-count chevron buttons in the expand column with a `GroupToggle` component that renders a descriptive label, an accessible `aria-label`, and a tooltip naming the grouping key (`session_id` or `parent_request_id`).
- Added a `TreeBranch` component that draws SVG-free tree lines (trunk, tick, closing branch) using absolutely-positioned `span` elements inside the expand cell, which is now `relative` and zero-padded so lines meet across rows.
- Extended `DisplayLogEntry` with `__turn`, `__isLast`, and `__parentIsLast` fields so the tree geometry knows which sibling is last and whether the outer session branch is still open at depth 2.
- `displayLogs` assembly now tracks turn numbers (root = turn 1, members count from 2) and passes `__isLast`/`__parentIsLast` down to `pushChain`.
- Session member rows receive a blue inset shadow (`#93c5fd` / `#1d4ed8`) instead of grey, distinguishing them from chain-child rows at a glance.
- The expand column widened from 52 px to 90 px to accommodate the text labels.
- Save buttons across multiple settings views (`cachingView`, `clientSettingsView`, `loggingView`, `mcpView`, `proxyView`) are now `sticky bottom-0` so they remain visible while scrolling long forms.
- MCP and Warp views narrowed their max-width from `max-w-7xl` to `max-w-4xl` for better readability.
- Several workspace page wrappers replaced `mx-auto max-w-7xl` with `no-padding-parent` to align with the layout convention used by sibling pages.
- The metric strip's six-column breakpoint dropped from `@6xl` to `@5xl` so the full strip appears sooner on laptop-sized windows.
- The recalculate-cost dialog's disabled button now shows a tooltip explaining why it is disabled ("All logs already have a cost", "No logs match the current filters", or a loading message).
- Added an E2E test suite (`Grouped View`) that mocks session and chain log data and asserts that the correct labels, tooltips, and nested rows appear after expanding each group type.

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
- [x] Refactor
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Chore/CI

## Affected areas

- [ ] Core (Go)
- [ ] Transports (HTTP)
- [ ] Providers/Integrations
- [ ] Plugins
- [x] UI (React)
- [ ] Docs

## How to test

```sh
cd ui
pnpm i
pnpm build

# Run the new E2E spec
pnpm exec playwright test tests/e2e/features/logs/logs.spec.ts --grep "Grouped View"
```

1. Navigate to `/workspace/logs?grouped=true` with traffic that has produced sessions and fallback chains.
2. Confirm session expanders show "N turns" and chain expanders show "N fallback(s)".
3. Hover each expander and verify the tooltip names `session_id` or `parent_request_id` respectively.
4. Expand a session row and confirm session member rows have a blue left border and show "turn 2", "turn 3", etc., while any fallback attempt under a member shows "fallback 1" with a grey border.
5. Open a settings page with a long form (e.g. Caching, Proxy) and scroll down; confirm the Save button stays pinned to the bottom.
6. Open the recalculate-cost dialog with no matching logs and hover the disabled Recalculate button; confirm the tooltip appears.

## Screenshots/Recordings

Before: expand column showed a bare number and a chevron for both sessions and chains, with no visual distinction between the two group types.

After: session rows show "N turns" with a blue left border on members; chain rows show "N fallback(s)" with grey borders; tree branch lines connect parents to children; save buttons are sticky on long settings forms.

## Breaking changes

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Related issues

## Security considerations

None. Changes are purely presentational and confined to the UI layer.

## Checklist

- [x] I read `docs/contributing/README.md` and followed the guidelines
- [x] I added/updated tests where appropriate
- [ ] I updated documentation where needed
- [x] I verified builds succeed (Go and UI)
- [x] I verified the CI pipeline passes locally if applicable

items.title: autodetect harness level session ids
items.body:
## Summary

Coding harnesses (Claude Code, Codex CLI, OpenCode) already send a session identifier on every request under their own header names. Previously, Bifrost only recognized `x-bf-session-id`, so harness traffic missed out on provider key stickiness and OTEL session grouping unless callers explicitly renamed their headers. This PR adds automatic fallback: when `x-bf-session-id` is absent, Bifrost adopts the first recognized harness session header it finds, in a defined priority order.

## Changes

- Added `MaxSessionIDLength = 255` constant to `core/schemas/useragents.go` and replaced all inline `255` literals with it so the cap is enforced consistently across every ingestion path (`x-bf-session-id`, baggage `session-id`, `x-bf-mcp-session-id`, and harness headers).
- Added `HarnessSessionHeaders` to `core/schemas/useragents.go`, listing the headers Claude Code, Codex CLI, and OpenCode send, in priority order, with inline rationale for what was deliberately excluded (`x-parent-session-id`, `x-qwen-code-session-id`).
- Added `ResolveHarnessSessionID(headers map[string]string)` in `transports/bifrost-http/lib/ctx.go` to walk the priority list and return the first non-empty, length-valid value.
- Added `ResolveSessionIDFromRequest(h *fasthttp.RequestHeader)` for callers that hold a raw fasthttp header (notably the tracing middleware, which runs before context conversion). It builds a lowercased header map itself so underscore-named Codex CLI headers are found regardless of fasthttp normalization.
- Updated `ConvertToBifrostContext` to run the harness fallback after the main header loop rather than inline, ensuring an explicit `x-bf-session-id` always wins even if a harness header appears first in the wire order.
- Updated the tracing middleware to call `ResolveSessionIDFromRequest` instead of peeking `x-bf-session-id` directly, so the `session.id` trace attribute and the key-stickiness session ID always agree.
- Fixed the providers sidebar in the UI: the configured-providers list is now the only scrolling region, the "Configured Providers" label and the "Add Provider" button are pinned outside the scroll area, and an empty-state illustration is shown when no providers are configured.
- Updated `docs/features/observability/otel.mdx` and `docs/providers/request-options.mdx` to document the harness fallback behavior and the full header priority table.

Notable design decisions:
- The fallback runs after the header loop rather than inside it to avoid a race where a harness header arriving before `x-bf-session-id` in iteration order would shadow the explicit value.
- Oversized harness session values are dropped (not truncated) and the next candidate in the priority list is tried, preventing an attacker-controlled value from becoming a KV lookup key or trace attribute.
- `x-parent-session-id` (OpenCode) is explicitly excluded because it would collapse every sub-agent onto its parent's key. `x-qwen-code-session-id` is excluded because it was designed but never shipped.

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Chore/CI

## Affected areas

- [x] Core (Go)
- [x] Transports (HTTP)
- [ ] Providers/Integrations
- [ ] Plugins
- [x] UI (React)
- [x] Docs

## How to test

```sh
go test ./transports/bifrost-http/lib/... -run TestConvertToBifrostContext_HarnessSessionHeaderFallback
go test ./transports/bifrost-http/lib/... -run TestConvertToBifrostContext_ExplicitSessionIDBeatsHarnessHeader
go test ./transports/bifrost-http/lib/... -run TestConvertToBifrostContext_HarnessSessionHeaderPriority
go test ./transports/bifrost-http/lib/... -run TestConvertToBifrostContext_OversizedHarnessSessionHeaderRejected
go test ./transports/bifrost-http/lib/... -run TestConvertToBifrostContext_MaxLengthHarnessSessionHeaderAccepted
go test ./transports/bifrost-http/lib/... -run TestResolveSessionIDFromRequest
go test ./transports/bifrost-http/lib/... -run TestSessionIDResolutionIsConsistent
go test ./...
```

To validate end-to-end: point a Claude Code or Codex CLI session at a Bifrost gateway without setting `x-bf-session-id`. Confirm that successive requests within the same agent run land on the same provider key and appear under a single `session.id` in the OTEL trace output.

## Screenshots/Recordings

**Providers sidebar — empty state (new)**

The sidebar now shows a "No providers configured yet" illustration when the list is empty, and the "Add Provider" button stays pinned at the bottom rather than scrolling away.

## Breaking changes

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Related issues

## Security considerations

Harness session header values are caller-controlled and flow into KV lookup keys and exported trace attributes. All ingestion paths enforce `MaxSessionIDLength = 255`; values exceeding this are dropped entirely (not truncated) and the next priority candidate is tried. Header values are never echoed in log output when they exceed the length cap.

## Checklist

- [x] I read `docs/contributing/README.md` and followed the guidelines
- [x] I added/updated tests where appropriate
- [x] I updated documentation where needed
- [x] I verified builds succeed (Go and UI)
- [ ] I verified the CI pipeline passes locally if applicable

items.title: feat(core): request-scoped provider credentials and base URL on BifrostRequest
items.body:
## Summary

Plugins that do dynamic user lookup and set provider/model configuration at runtime need to supply the credential and endpoint for a request. Today that only works when the provider is statically configured and the credential is in its key pool. This PR adds methods on `BifrostRequest` that a plugin calls from `PreRequestHook` (and, to vary it per attempt, from `PreLLMHook`). The attempt then runs against that configuration without the provider being configured, and leaves nothing behind.

## Changes

- `BifrostRequest.UpdateProviderKey`, `UpdateProviderBaseURL`, `UpdateProviderAllowPrivateNetwork` and `ProviderOverrideFor`. Configuration is keyed by provider, so fallbacks to other providers carry their own credentials and a credential always follows its provider. Calling them from `PreLLMHook` changes the configuration for the attempt about to run of a request that already carries some, which covers two fallbacks to the same provider with different keys or endpoints. Keys must hold literal values (`env.`/`vault.` references are rejected); base URLs are shape-checked without parsing or DNS.
- An attempt whose provider has request-scoped configuration runs in the calling goroutine instead of going through a provider queue. It uses a shared instance per provider type and private-network policy, created on first use with default network settings and never registered, listed or given workers. An attempt carries no per-instance concurrency cap: with no queue or workers behind the instance, a cap would only make attempts past it wait or fail however much capacity the process had. Each attempt runs in its caller's goroutine and is bounded by the caller's admission, the request context and the attempt timeout. The per-message body of `requestWorker` moves into `processChannelMessage` in its own commit so both paths share it; hide whitespace to review.
- The request-scoped key goes through the existing fixed-key path, so retries, attempt records and routing info work as for a pinned key; it is never looked up in, checked against or added to configured keys. The account is not consulted, and session affinity is skipped for these requests.
- Optional `schemas.RequestScopedProvider` interface: `ForRequest(requestType, key, baseURL)` validates the configuration and returns the receiver, or a shallow copy sharing its HTTP clients when there is a base URL (one allocation). Implemented by OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Cohere, Cerebras, Groq, Mistral, Nebius, OpenRouter, Parasail, Perplexity, xAI, Replicate, Hugging Face, Ollama and SGL; by vLLM (endpoint on the key); by Azure (API key and endpoint only, no service principal or batch results) and by Bedrock (API key or static keys in a checked region, no role assumption or endpoint overrides, files and batches need static keys). Providers without it fail closed.
- Fail-closed: unsupported providers and auth modes are rejected rather than falling back to configured keys or ambient credentials.
- A request without request-scoped configuration resolves its provider queue before `PreLLMHook` exactly as today, with the same error for an unconfigured provider. A request that carries configuration only does the lock-free queue lookup there; for a provider without a queue the decision waits until after the hooks (request-scoped path if the attempt now has configuration, otherwise the queue is created as before, and a lookup failure reaches `PostLLMHook`). For such requests, fallbacks to providers without static configuration are not skipped up front, since `PreLLMHook` may configure them.
- `BatchCreateRequest` keeps its provider check, which runs before any plugin, so a request-scoped batch create still needs a provider that check accepts.
- Cost: requests that don't use this pay a few length/nil checks and no allocations (configured chat completion against a local server: 165 allocs/request unary and 207–209 streamed, on `dev` and on this branch). Requests that use it allocate no more than a configured request (164 unary, 207–209 stream in `BenchmarkRequestScopedChatCompletion`, against 165 and 207–209 configured). Instance lookup and `ForRequest` without a base URL allocate nothing; updating an existing entry allocates nothing; the first `Update*` call per provider allocates the entry, and each request-scoped attempt allocates a copy of its key. `BifrostRequest` grows by one slice header (448 → 472 bytes, so the 448-byte size class becomes 480); the pooled `ChannelMessage` grows by that and one pointer (536 → 568 bytes, still the 576-byte size class).

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Chore/CI

## Affected areas

- [x] Core (Go)
- [ ] Transports (HTTP)
- [x] Providers/Integrations
- [ ] Plugins
- [ ] UI (React)
- [x] Docs

## How to test

```sh
cd core
go test ./... -race -count=1
go test -run '^$' -bench BenchmarkRequestScopedChatCompletion -benchmem .
```

New tests run requests against providers with no static configuration using httptest servers. They check that no queue, worker, provider entry, key or config lookup, or session-affinity state is created; that no goroutine is left behind and the configuration is released after the request; that per-attempt credentials (including two attempts against the same provider type) and fallbacks to other providers each reach only their own endpoint; that unsupported configurations, private and loopback destinations without opt-in, and link-local destinations fail without a provider call and are observed by `PostLLMHook`; that a request without request-scoped configuration still fails on an unconfigured provider before the LLM hooks, and `BatchCreateRequest` still checks its provider before `PreRequestHook`; and that 64 goroutines with distinct credentials never cross. A table test builds every `RequestScopedProvider` implementer the way core does and pins `ForRequest`'s allocations and rules, and that each one refuses loopback unless private networks are allowed. A reflection test sets every `SecretVar` reachable from `Key` to an `env.` and a `vault.` reference and checks `UpdateProviderKey` rejects it, so a field added later cannot be missed.

This adds no provider-harness case: the feature is reachable only from a Go plugin, not from an HTTP request.

## Breaking changes

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Related issues

Closes #2029

## Security considerations

Request-scoped configuration is never serialized or written to the context, and is released with the request. Destinations are checked at dial time: link-local addresses are always refused, and RFC 1918 and loopback addresses need `UpdateProviderAllowPrivateNetwork` (loopback is treated as private for these instances only, through `NetworkConfig.LoopbackIsPrivate`, which is runtime-only). Keys must carry literal values. Auth modes that would use ambient credentials or per-credential caches are rejected. WebSocket and realtime endpoints do not take request-scoped configuration.
